result.summary: Two single-commit diffs across two repos land Phase 1 of the E4-XML "Andockung" (#230). CE commit 698977fe (6 files) adds a new GoF Facade module libs/cache_engine/builder/profile_facade/: a POD-only header profile_run_facade.hpp (STL-only ProfileRunArgs/ProfileRunResult; no umbrella/CompileFn/mp11 in the signature) plus the single umbrella-pulling TU profile_run_facade.cpp, which maps the POD args field-by-field onto tlz::RunProfileArgs, builds a real g++-16 response-file (@rsp) CompileFn writing a .rsp then invoking `g++-16 @"rsp" > log 2>&1` via std::system with measurement defines (COMDARE_ANATOMY_MODULE_BUILD/MEASUREMENT_ON/CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS/EXPERIMENT_MODE_ON plus OS/arch/cache-line macros), discovers Achse-2 XML load-profiles from load_profile_dir, calls tlz::run_profile, and copies back the result including any_measured/any_resumed. Its new CMakeLists.txt declares a STATIC EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL target with PUBLIC=slim-header / PRIVATE=heavy-includes isolation, links Boost::mp11 + xml_config_parser + workload_driver + anatomy_module_loader PRIVATE, registers itself on the GLOBAL COMDARE_PAPER_CODEGEN_CONSUMER_TARGETS property for codegen ordering, and bakes a '|'-joined default include set (incl. vendored boost_mp11) into COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES; the perm include set is derived from PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR/PROJECT_BINARY_DIR globs. builder/CMakeLists.txt adds add_subdirectory(profile_facade), and anatomy_module_loader + workload_driver CMakeLists switch CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR->PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR for correct -I paths in the super sub-build (claimed No-Op standalone). Super commit 5b5dc9c (3 files) adds to Code/02_messung_driver/main.cpp a COMDARE_MESSUNG_HAVE_E4_FACADE-guarded, COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1-opt-in block that runs the facade against a thesis profile (env COMDARE_THESIS_PROFILE > CMake default m3v2_study.profile.xml, with COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR / COMDARE_E4_CAP overrides) and otherwise falls through unchanged to the classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C path; CMakeLists.txt conditionally links comdare::profile_run_facade behind if(TARGET ...) and sets the guard + default-profile defines; and the ce submodule gitlink is bumped 8c73ef7->698977f.
result.conventions: No CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md applies to any changed file: the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md does not exist, neither repo root has one, and no ancestor directory of any changed file contains one. The only CLAUDE.md in either tree is ce/ext/allocator/A01-hoard/CLAUDE.md, which is not an ancestor of the changed files (they live under libs/cache_engine/builder/{profile_facade,anatomy_module_loader,workload_driver} and super Code/02_messung_driver/), so it is out of scope. However, the project conventions the reviewer needs are carried in the user's auto-memory (MEMORY.md, supplied in-context), and this commit explicitly claims to honor several as HARD REQUIREMENTS: (1) additive-only + golden/ABI-neutral - must NOT touch permutation_axes.xml, golden_fullpilot_320, ABI-MAJOR, POD sizeof, or GenusBindingTraits (feedback_messdaten_nie_loeschen_abi_darf_brechen, feedback_never_delete_documentation); (2) NO runtime-switch/vtable in the hot path - String->Type dispatch must stay compile-time behind the .cpp umbrella boundary (feedback_no_runtime_switch, feedback_compile_time_only_no_runtime, feedback_crtp_concept_guard_mix_pattern); (3) only named textbook design patterns + zero-cost metaprogramming - the change bills itself as GoF Facade (feedback_lehrbuch_design_patterns_only_zero_cost_metaprog, reference_meta_driven_concept_hardening_pattern); (4) NO Python anywhere in the build chain - CMake functions + sh/bat + C++ helpers only (feedback_no_python_in_buildchain); (5) build/CI scripts must be POSIX-portable (no grep -oP) and any XML the buildsystem parses is literal grep/awk-parsed, so & must not be escaped (reference_buildsystem_scripts_posix_no_grep_p, reference_buildsystem_xml_grep_parsed_not_strict_xml) - relevant since the facade shells out g++-16 via std::system with a bare-string command. Also note buildsystem.xml is hands-off (owned by a separate agent; only CMake/CI references may be fixed) and cold-build g++-16 ICE segfaults are known transient infra, not code (reference_ci_runner_ice_cold_cache_instability). Reviewer focus per the request: facade field-mapping correctness (incl. RunProfileResult any_measured/any_resumed), @rsp CompileFn + std::system call safety and path-injection in the quoted rsp/source/output/log paths, resource/lifetime of the captured-by-value lambda and the ofstream rsp scope, PUBLIC-vs-PRIVATE include isolation, EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, the COMDARE_PAPER_CODEGEN_CONSUMER_TARGETS codegen-ordering property, the '|'-joined COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES, and whether the opt-in E4 dock can ever break the classic ExperimentDriver fallback.

candidates.summary: The Achse-2 'COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR set but 0 valid profiles -> hard abort' guard (run_lazy_150.cpp:201-205, 'Achse 2 darf nicht still entfallen') is dropped, even though line 129 claims parity with run_lazy_150.cpp:193-206 which contains that guard.
candidates.failure_scenario: Operator launches the opt-in multi-day E4 run (COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1) with COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR pointing at a mistyped/wrong dir, or one whose XMLs all fail parse_load_profile's strict <op_mix> validation. The harness would abort immediately (exit 4). The facade silently proceeds with an empty workload_registry; run_profile then skips the workload-axis injection (profile_run_entry.hpp:132), so every emitted CSV row goes through the fixed-workload run_observable_perm fallback with two_phase_valid=0 -- the entire multi-day measurement is scientifically invalid and this is only discovered after it finishes.

candidates.summary: The E4 dock never sets pa.min_free_gb and exposes no env/arg to enable RAM admission; the successor to run_lazy_150 (which took min_free_gb via argv[7]) hardcodes the default 0.0 (admission OFF).
candidates.failure_scenario: On a memory-constrained cluster node the E4 dock runs ~4 parallel g++-16 umbrella compiles (all 19 axis types, multi-GB each) with RAM admission disabled and no way to turn it on. Free RAM is exhausted, the OOM-killer terminates a g++ or messung_driver itself, aborting or corrupting the multi-day run -- exactly the failure the harness let operators gate via min_free_gb.

candidates.summary: COMDARE_PLATFORM / COMDARE_BUILD_VERSION CSV-tag overrides (wired in run_lazy_150.cpp:274-276 to platform_override / build_version_tag_override) are not wired in the E4 dock, so rows fall back to the profile's default platform/build tag.
candidates.failure_scenario: The infra measurement host sets COMDARE_PLATFORM/COMDARE_BUILD_VERSION per node to tag CSV rows for the AMD(prod1)/Intel(prod2) SIMD matrix (#276/#13). The E4 dock ignores both env vars, so rows measured on different platforms all carry the same profile-default platform tag -- the platform dimension becomes indistinguishable/mislabeled when the CSVs are merged, silently corrupting the cross-platform comparison.

candidates.summary: The compile invocation is a bare single std::system() call; the harness CompileFn wrapped the equivalent call in run_cl_with_c1083_retry (retry on transient compile failure), and that retry-on-transient behavior is not re-established.
candidates.failure_scenario: A transient g++-16 ICE segfault (the documented cold-cache flake, reference_ci_runner_ice_cold_cache_instability) hits one perm_<id>.cpp during a ~320-binary run. std::system returns non-zero once and there is no retry, so that binary is a permanent hole/failure in the CSV, forcing a manual re-run of the multi-day measurement. (Lower confidence: the harness retry was marker-scoped to Windows OneDrive locks, so a Linux ICE was never explicitly retried there either.)

candidates.summary: The E4 dock never sets pa.run_sota_series and provides no COMDARE_RUN_SOTA opt-out; the harness honored env COMDARE_RUN_SOTA=0 (run_lazy_150.cpp:269-270) to disable the SOTA-series passes, so the dock always runs them.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator wanting a basis-only (re)measurement has no way to skip the SOTA-series passes; the E4 dock always builds and measures every declared <sota_series> tier, adding unrequested multi-day compute (and rebuilding SOTA binaries) to a run that only needed the basis-320 subset.

candidates.summary: An uncaught exception in the opt-in E4 block (throwing std::filesystem::create_directories(e4_dir) at 496 and the entirely unguarded run_profile_facade(pa) at 512) unwinds main and skips the classic ExperimentDriver fallback the comment promises always runs.
candidates.failure_scenario: With COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 and a valid profile, if e4_dir cannot be created (output_dir on a read-only mount, or a path component is a regular file) create_directories(e4_dir) at line 496 uses the THROWING overload and throws std::filesystem::filesystem_error; it is uncaught, so main() aborts via std::terminate and the classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C measurement path (documented 'laeuft dennoch weiter (additiv)') never executes -- the whole messung_driver dies producing no measurements. Same outcome for any throw (std::bad_alloc while building the 320-tree, DLL-load/filesystem errors) escaping run_profile_facade(pa) at line 512, directly contradicting the 'additiv, bricht KEINEN bestehenden Lauf' invariant.

candidates.summary: std::system's POSIX return value is an encoded wait-status, not the process exit code, but is returned raw as the CompileFn result and then rendered downstream as the compile exit code.
candidates.failure_scenario: On the target Linux/g++-16 platform, a perm_<id>.cpp that fails to compile with exit code 1 makes std::system return 256 (1<<8); build_orchestrator.hpp:310 stores that in BuildResult.status and logs message 'compile-exit 256' (a g++ ICE killed by SIGSEGV -- a known transient on this project -- shows as ~35584). Anyone triaging a failed tier binary sees a meaningless encoded number instead of the real exit code 1, and any tooling that keys on specific compile exit codes misfires. (The status==0 success/failure test itself stays correct because raw 0 iff the child exited 0.)

candidates.summary: The g++ shell command is assembled by string concatenation with only double-quote wrapping of the response-file and log paths (both derived from the configured measurement output directory), so shell metacharacters in that path break or inject into the invocation.
candidates.failure_scenario: If the measurement output directory contains a double quote, $, or backtick (e.g. an operator points output at a path like /data/run"1 or one containing $(...)), the constructed command `g++-16 @"..." > "..." 2>&1` passed to std::system is mis-tokenized by /bin/sh: every perm build fails (zero usable tier binaries for the whole E4 run), or an embedded $(cmd)/backtick executes an arbitrary command during the measurement. Double-quote wrapping guards spaces but not these metacharacters.

candidates.summary: std::strtoull for COMDARE_E4_CAP is used with no endptr/errno validation and can silently produce 0 or a truncated value.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator sets COMDARE_E4_CAP to a malformed value ('auto', '1k', a typo) intending to cap the build; strtoull returns 0, so pa.max_binaries=0 silently means 'use the profile's full <run_options>.cap' and the driver builds far more tier binaries than intended (a multi-day build kicked off unbounded). An out-of-range value yields ULLONG_MAX with errno=ERANGE ignored, and on a 32-bit-size_t target (RISC-V build in the platform matrix) the unsigned-long-long result narrows/truncates into std::size_t max_binaries.

candidates.summary: COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML is compared exactly against the string "1", so common truthy spellings and trailing whitespace leave the opt-in inactive.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator or CI sets COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML to 'true', 'yes', or '1\n'/'1 ' (a trailing newline/space when sourced from a file); std::string_view{e4_flag} == "1" is false, so want_e4 stays false and the E4-XML #229 measurement silently never starts -- only the classic ExperimentDriver path runs, with just an 'INAKTIV' log line and no indication the intended run was skipped.

candidates.summary: COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 runs the facade E4 chain but then falls through (no return/skip) into the full classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C path; there is no E4-only mode.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator sets COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 to run the (per the comments multi-day, cluster) XML measurement. run_profile_facade() returns and the block ends at #endif with no early-out, so main() continues into the classic ExperimentDriver measurement (load_messreihen / external_specs, line 526+). If external measurement specs are configured (the normal state of messung_driver), the process performs the entire classic measurement pipeline afterward, doing large unintended extra work and emitting classic outputs alongside e4_xml_profile/measurements.csv. Enabling E4 can never run E4 in isolation.

candidates.summary: The super-sub-build -I fix (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR -> PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR) is applied only to workload_driver + anatomy_module_loader; sibling builder modules pruef_dock and anatomy_codegen_tool still use CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR.
candidates.failure_scenario: This is a general defect (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR is the super root in an add_subdirectory sub-build) patched at two instances rather than generalized. libs/cache_engine/builder/pruef_dock/CMakeLists.txt:11-13 and anatomy_codegen_tool/CMakeLists.txt:10-22 still hard-code ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/cache_engine/... in their PUBLIC include dirs. The next super-sub-build consumer that links either module gets -I pointing at <super-root>/libs/cache_engine (nonexistent) -> C1083/'No such file' on its public headers. A shared helper/variable for the ce include root would fix the class, not two symptoms.

candidates.summary: make_gpp_compile_fn re-implements the response-file (@rsp) compile-fn pattern that already exists as build_orchestrator.hpp make_system_compile_fn and is copy-pasted in run_lazy_150.cpp/test_sota_series_pilot.cpp/test_axis_sweep_pilot.cpp.
candidates.failure_scenario: build_orchestrator.hpp:353 already hosts make_system_compile_fn as the designated CompileFn factory (MSVC variant), and the identical @rsp+std::system+.log structure is duplicated in run_lazy_150.cpp:234-249 and two thesis_tiere pilots. Now a 4th+ copy exists. Any fix to the shared logic (rsp quoting, added mess-define, diagnostics flag, exit-status handling) must be replicated in every copy or they silently diverge; the correct home is a make_gpp_compile_fn factory in build_orchestrator that the facade and harness share.

candidates.summary: The topics/*/axis_* + axes/* -> generated-dir glob/foreach is a near-verbatim copy of tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:11-30 (COMDARE_ALL_AXIS_GENERATED_DIRS), diverging only in CMAKE_BINARY_DIR vs PROJECT_BINARY_DIR.
candidates.failure_scenario: The generated-axis-include derivation now lives in two places with a deliberate but easy-to-forget PROJECT_BINARY_DIR vs CMAKE_BINARY_DIR difference. If the axis directory layout or the generated/topics|axes path convention changes, both copies must be updated in lock-step; missing one yields C1083 on generated axis_*_flags.hpp in whichever target (tests vs facade) wasn't updated. A shared cmake function returning the generated-dir list (parameterized on the binary-dir base) would prevent the drift.

candidates.summary: The load-profile discovery loop (discover_load_profiles/parse_load_profile -> registry+values) is copy-pasted from run_lazy_150.cpp:193-206.
candidates.failure_scenario: Achse-2 discovery is now maintained in two independent places. run_lazy_150.cpp treats 'COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR set but 0 valid profiles' as a hard abort (return 4, 'darf nicht still entfallen'); the facade copy silently produces an empty registry and drops the workload axis. A future change to load-profile parsing/validation must be mirrored by hand; a shared discover_workload_registry(dir)->{registry,values} helper would keep them consistent.

candidates.summary: The production facade library reaches into the test tree: it adds ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/unit/thesis_tiere to its PRIVATE include set and bakes it into COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES.
candidates.failure_scenario: A 'produktive Fassade' and every emitted perm.cpp sub-compile depend on headers under tests/unit/thesis_tiere (profile_run_entry.hpp/source_catalog.hpp/sota_catalog.hpp). If that test directory is ever relocated, pruned, or excluded from a packaging/install/non-test build, both the facade TU and every E4 perm.cpp @rsp compile fail with C1083. The library->tests dependency direction is an altitude smell (acknowledged Phase-1 debt in the header comment, to be lifted into a production location later).

candidates.summary: The opt-in E4 call pf::run_profile_facade(pa) is not wrapped in try/catch and main() has no top-level exception handler, so any exception from the heavy XML-driven run aborts the whole process.
candidates.failure_scenario: With COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 and a valid thesis profile, if tlz::run_profile throws during the multi-day run (e.g. AnatomyModuleLoader dlopen/load failure, a std::filesystem_error on the cluster such as disk-full/permission, or a std::stoull/stod parse exception on measurement data), the uncaught exception triggers std::terminate and messung_driver aborts. The classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C measurement at line 525+ then never runs and emits no output — directly contradicting the line-519 comment 'klassischer ExperimentDriver-Pfad laeuft dennoch weiter (additiv)'. The code only continues-on-trouble for a non-zero exit_code return (lines 517-519), never for an exception.

candidates.summary: The opt-in guard calls the throwing overload std::filesystem::exists(thesis_profile); an OS error (not merely 'file missing') throws and, with no try/catch in main, aborts the process before either measurement path runs.
candidates.failure_scenario: With COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 and COMDARE_THESIS_PROFILE (or the CMake default) resolving under a directory that lacks search/execute permission (EACCES) or is otherwise unstattable, std::filesystem::exists throws std::filesystem_error instead of returning false. Uncaught, messung_driver terminates at the guard itself — before running the E4 dock and before the classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C path — so a mere profile-path permission problem crashes the driver and produces no measurement at all.

candidates.summary: E4 dock compiles/measures on Linux with g++-16 but never sets ProfileRunArgs::platform_override, so run_profile stamps every CSV row with the profile's platform="win-x86_64" (m3v2_study.profile.xml:145 -> profile_run_entry.hpp:144-149,201).
candidates.failure_scenario: Operator runs COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 on Linux (prod1) with the default m3v2_study profile: output_dir/e4_xml_profile/measurements.csv rows all carry platform=win-x86_64 even though every perm_<id>.so was built and measured by g++-16 on Linux, silently mis-attributing Linux/g++ measurements to Windows in the primary thesis dataset (platform dimension corrupted, no error surfaced).

candidates.summary: perm_include_dirs() resolves the g++ include set through the global env COMDARE_PILOT_INCLUDES in preference to the facade's own CMake-baked COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES, so a stale/foreign value in the environment silently replaces the correct include set (wrapper routing through a global instead of its own state).
candidates.failure_scenario: The measurement host or a leftover thesis_tiere shell exports COMDARE_PILOT_INCLUDES with Windows/cl-style or otherwise mismatched ';'-separated paths (the header comment states the infra host sets this per platform); the facade ignores its correct baked includes (incl. vendored boost/mp11) and hands those to g++-16, so every perm_<id>.cpp @rsp compile fails with 'boost/mp11: No such file', zero binaries build, measurements.csv is header-only and run returns exit_code=1.

candidates.summary: The opt-in E4 block calls run_profile_facade (and std::filesystem::exists throwing overload at line 490) with no try/catch, and main() has none either, so an exception during an opted-in E4 run skips the classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C fallback that follows the block.
candidates.failure_scenario: With COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1, an I/O error (disk full while writing the CSV/.rsp, or a permission/not-a-directory error on the profile path making std::filesystem::exists throw) propagates out of run_profile_facade/exists() through main (no handler) -> std::terminate; the classic ExperimentDriver A/B/C path below never runs, breaking the commit's stated 'klassischer Pfad laeuft dennoch weiter (additiv)' fallback guarantee.

candidates.summary: The opt-in E4-XML block has no exception handling, so a throw from run_profile_facade skips the classic ExperimentDriver fallback that the block explicitly guarantees.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator runs messung_driver with COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 and a valid thesis profile. Deep inside pf::run_profile_facade -> tlz::run_profile -> BuildOrchestrator (a multi-hour/day DLL build + measurement chain that dlopens modules, writes many files, allocates large buffers) a std::filesystem_error / std::bad_alloc / loader exception is thrown. The E4 block (and main) have no try/catch, so the exception propagates out of main() and std::terminate aborts the process BEFORE the classic A/B/C ExperimentDriver path at lines 524+ ever runs. That invocation produces no classic measurement results at all, directly contradicting the code's own promise at line 519 ('klassischer ExperimentDriver-Pfad laeuft dennoch weiter (additiv)') and the commit's additive/fallback guarantee. Only exit_code!=0 is handled (lines 517-519); exceptions are not. Same gap applies to the throwing std::filesystem::create_directories(e4_dir) at line 496.

candidates.summary: COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES only appends Boost.MP11 when the vendored tree exists, so a FetchContent-provided mp11 is silently dropped from the self-contained perm sub-compile include set.
candidates.failure_scenario: On a machine/config where the vendored cmake/third_party/boost_mp11 directory is absent and Boost.MP11 is instead resolved via FetchContent (the documented fallback in cmake/boost_mp11_setup.cmake, whose real include dir is ${boost_mp11_SOURCE_DIR}/include, not under cmake/third_party), the if(EXISTS "${_facade_mp11_inc}/boost/mp11.hpp") guard at line 91 is false. The baked COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES then omits any mp11 include dir. At runtime, with COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 and COMDARE_PILOT_INCLUDES unset, perm_include_dirs() returns that mp11-less list, so every emitted perm_<id>.cpp (which pulls all_axes_umbrella -> boost/mp11) fails the g++-16 @rsp sub-compile with 'boost/mp11.hpp: No such file or directory'. run_profile builds zero tier DLLs and returns exit_code=1 with no measurements, even though the facade lib itself linked fine (it links Boost::mp11 directly, masking the gap in the separate perm sub-compile).

verdicts.evidence: Line 484 confirms the strict match: `bool const want_e4 = (e4_flag != nullptr && std::string_view{e4_flag} == "1");` — so `=true`, `=yes`, or trailing-whitespace values (`"1\n"`, `"1 "`) yield want_e4==false and the E4-XML block (lines 494-520) is skipped. Mechanism is real and correctly located. Trigger is uncertain/env-dependent, however: the documented contract (comment lines 467-468 and the log line itself) is explicitly `COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1`, so under documented usage it works; the bug only fires if an operator/CI sets a non-canonical value or introduces whitespace (plausible via file-sourced env, but not guaranteed). The 'silently ... no indication' framing is also partly inaccurate: lines 487-488 print `[#230] ... VERFUEGBAR, aber INAKTIV (Opt-in: env COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1). Standard bleibt ExperimentDriver A/B/C.`, which is a non-silent notice that even restates the correct `=1` value. Would be CONFIRMED given evidence that an actual CI job/operator sets the var to something other than exactly "1".

The guard IS present in run_lazy_150.cpp:201-205 ('if (workload_values.empty()) { std::cerr << "...0 gueltige Profile...Abbruch (Achse 2 darf nicht still entfallen)."; return 4; }') inside the COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR block (193-206). The facade drops it: profile_run_facade.cpp:132-141 runs the identical discover_load_profiles/parse_load_profile loop but the 'if (!args.load_profile_dir.empty())' block closes at line 141 after only the std::cout log -- no empty-check, no abort. Yet line 129 explicitly claims parity: 'Gleiche Discovery wie run_lazy_150.cpp:193-206, aber POD-getrieben', i.e. the range that contains the guard at 201-205. The downstream harm is confirmed: profile_run_entry.hpp:132 gates workload-axis injection on 'if (!a.workload_values.empty())', and its own comment (127-128) states that without it the iterator falls to run_observable_perm so 'JEDE Zeile two_phase_valid=0 (Mess-UNGUELTIG)'. Silence is confirmed: profile_run_entry.hpp:328 sets 'res.exit_code = ((res.any_measured > 0 || res.any_resumed > 0) && csv_ok) ? 0 : 1', so measurements still run and exit 0 is returned; the facade copies it (out.exit_code=r.exit_code) and super main.cpp only warns 'if (rr.exit_code != 0)'. Trigger: COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 plus a mistyped/wrong COMDARE_LOAD_PROFILE_DIR (super main.cpp:96-97 maps env -> pa.load_profile_dir) or a dir whose XMLs all fail parse -> workload_values empty -> run_lazy_150 would exit 4 but the facade proceeds and yields an invalid multi-day dataset detectable only post-hoc.

main.cpp E4 block (super 5b5dc9c) sets pa.profile_path/out_csv/src_dir/dll_dir/build_version and conditionally load_profile_dir/max_binaries, but never pa.run_sota_series. The POD default is true (profile_run_facade.hpp: 'bool run_sota_series = true;'), and the facade forwards it unchanged (profile_run_facade.cpp: 'a.run_sota_series = args.run_sota_series;'). run_profile gates all SOTA passes on it (profile_run_entry.hpp:284 'if (a.run_sota_series) {'). The env opt-out lives ONLY in the harness caller (run_lazy_150.cpp:269-270: 'if (char const* rs = std::getenv("COMDARE_RUN_SOTA"); rs != nullptr && std::string{rs} == "0") a.run_sota_series = false;'), and grep for COMDARE_RUN_SOTA across the ce repo finds it only in run_lazy_150.cpp + docs — run_profile does not read it internally, and the new dock reads only COMDARE_THESIS_PROFILE/RUN_E4_XML/LOAD_PROFILE_DIR/E4_CAP. Default profile m3v2_study.profile.xml declares 24 <sota_series> entries, so COMDARE_RUN_E4_XML=1 always builds/measures every SOTA tier with no way to suppress them (COMDARE_RUN_SOTA=0 is silently ignored on the dock path).

Verified duplication: facade CMakeLists.txt:17-30 and tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:11-30 are structurally identical (same GLOB of "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/cache_engine/topics/*/axis_*", same IS_DIRECTORY + file(RELATIVE_PATH ... topics ...) -> generated/topics/${rel}, same axes/* glob -> get_filename_component NAME -> generated/axes/${name}). The ONLY semantic divergence is the binary-dir base: tests uses "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated/topics/${_axis_rel}" (line 19) and "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated/axes/${_axes_name}" (line 28), whereas facade uses "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/topics/${_rel}" (line 21) and "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/axes/${_n}" (line 28) -- exactly as the candidate states (rest is trivial var renaming _comdare_*->_facade_*). So the near-verbatim-copy claim is factually confirmed. The failure (C1083 on generated axis_*_flags.hpp) is contingent: both copies currently compute correct dirs and build fine; the break only occurs if a FUTURE edit changes the topics|axes/generated path convention and updates only one of the two blocks. Mechanism real, trigger is a future maintenance event of uncertain timing -> PLAUSIBLE. What would confirm: a later commit altering the axis-layout/generated-path convention that touches only one block, yielding C1083 in the un-updated target. The suggested fix (a shared cmake function parameterized on the binary-dir base) is valid since the divergence is precisely that base.

main.cpp has 0 try and 0 catch (grep -c both return 0; main spans lines 217-611), so no top-level handler exists. profile_run_facade.cpp:118-119: cmd = cxx + " @\"" + rsp + "\" > \"" + log + "\" 2>&1" then 'return std::system(cmd.c_str());' — shell redirection forces std::system through /bin/sh -c, whose POSIX/glibc return value is the shell's wait-status, not the exit code, and it is returned raw as the CompileFn result. build_orchestrator.hpp:309 stores it raw ('r.status = compile_(job);') and line 310 renders it verbatim: 'r.message = (r.status == 0) ? "ok" : ("compile-exit " + std::to_string(r.status));'. For a g++ compile error (exit 1) the shell exits 1, so the wait-status is 1<<8 = 256 -> 'compile-exit 256'; for a g++ ICE killed by SIGSEGV the shell exits 128+11=139, so wait-status is 139<<8 = 35584 -> 'compile-exit 35584' — exactly the two numbers the candidate names. Anyone triaging a failed tier binary sees the encoded wait-status instead of the real exit code. The success/failure test is unaffected as the candidate notes: BuildResult::ok() at build_orchestrator.hpp:91 is 'return status == 0;', and the raw wait-status is 0 iff the shell exited 0 iff g++ succeeded. No WEXITSTATUS/WIFEXITED decoding exists anywhere in libs/ or the thesis_tiere harness (grep returned nothing).

But this is the documented, intended design, not a defect: the header comment states the dock is 'ADDITIV & OPT-IN' and that 'Diese Andockung bricht KEINEN bestehenden Lauf' (lines 466-470), and line 519 reiterates the classic path 'laeuft dennoch weiter (additiv)'. Running E4 in addition to the classic path is the whole point of 'additiv'; skipping the classic path would 'break the existing run', the opposite of the stated intent. There is no correctness malfunction: E4 writes to output_dir/e4_xml_profile/ (line 495) while the classic path writes to output_dir/<spec.id> or output_dir/A|B|C (lines 544/586) — disjoint outputs, no shared state corrupted. The finding's 'unintended extra work' framing is contradicted by the explicit additive documentation, so the defect claim is refuted.

candidates.summary: The facade's PRIVATE link/include set omits the ~15 vendored allocator/paper adapter targets (comdare::adapter::a04_mimalloc..a11, p07..p30) whose usage-requirement include dirs supply <mimalloc.h> and the other vendored headers that all_axes_umbrella transitively #includes, so the facade's own umbrella TU fails to compile in the super sub-build.
candidates.failure_scenario: In the super build messung_driver links comdare::profile_run_facade, so the facade compiles profile_run_facade.cpp -> profile_run_entry.hpp -> source_catalog.hpp -> all_axes_umbrella.hpp -> axis_06_allocator_registry -> axis_06_allocator_mimalloc -> <mimalloc.h>. Because target_link_libraries lists only Boost::mp11 + xml_config_parser + workload_driver + anatomy_module_loader (not the a04_mimalloc..a11 / p07..p30 adapter targets that carry the vendored include dirs, the way test_v31_adapters at tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:277-301 does), g++ errors 'mimalloc.h: No such file or directory' and the analyse:thesis-data super-CI job goes red (this exact failure is documented in the later super revert fac49e66). Standalone-ce hid it because the facade is EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and was only ever built via an explicit --target where those adapter include dirs happened to be present globally, and the smoke targets it claims parity with (m3v2_pmc_smoke) only compile the umbrella under a config where the codegen-gated allocator path is inactive.

candidates.summary: COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES (the -I set baked for the RUNTIME g++ @rsp compile of every emitted perm_<id>.cpp) is derived solely from the same incomplete _facade_heavy_includes (+mp11) and therefore also lacks the vendored adapter include dirs, so the actual E4 tier-binary builds cannot find <mimalloc.h>; fixing the link libraries (finding at line 72) does NOT populate this baked path, so it is a second, independent break.
candidates.failure_scenario: During an opted-in E4 run, make_gpp_compile_fn (profile_run_facade.cpp) writes an @rsp whose include flags come from perm_include_dirs() = split(COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES,'|'). Each emitted perm_<id>.cpp #includes all_axes_umbrella -> <mimalloc.h>, which is absent from the baked set (set(_facade_perm_inc ${_facade_heavy_includes}) only adds vendored mp11, never the adapter include dirs). g++ fails, the error is redirected into the per-binary .cxx.log, std::system returns nonzero, and run_profile builds zero tier binaries (measured=resumed=0, exit_code=1) even after the line-72 link fix, because target INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES are not reflected into this compile-define string.

verdicts.evidence: The claim's mechanism 'all_axes_umbrella -> <mimalloc.h>' is factually wrong. <mimalloc.h> has exactly ONE include site in libs/cache_engine (axes/alloc/vendor_includes/mimalloc_include.hpp:22) and it is guarded: line 20 '#if COMDARE_AXIS_06_USE_MIMALLOC' / line 22 '#include <mimalloc.h>' / '#else' -> no-op forward stubs. COMDARE_AXIS_06_USE_MIMALLOC = ENABLE && HAVE (CMakeLists.txt:655-658) and resolves to 0 in ALL actual build configs: build*/generated/axes/alloc/axis_06_allocator_flags.hpp:25 = '#define COMDARE_AXIS_06_USE_MIMALLOC 0' (4/4 configs). The perm compile does not set this macro (perm_mess_defines() in profile_run_facade.cpp emits only COMDARE_ANATOMY_MODULE_BUILD + 3 mess defines + OS/arch macros); the value comes from the generated flags header, which the baked set CAN resolve because _facade_heavy_includes contains '${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/generated' (CMakeLists.txt:44) and <axes/alloc/axis_06_allocator_flags.hpp> lives under generated/. Thus USE_MIMALLOC=0 -> the #else stub branch is taken -> <mimalloc.h> is never #included -> its include dir (ext/allocator/A04-mimalloc/include) is not needed. Corroboration: the proven umbrella-compiling reference targets the facade mirrors, m3v2_pmc_smoke/test_harness_compile (tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:2127-2134), ALSO omit the mimalloc include dir and link only Boost::mp11 yet compile the umbrella - only possible because USE_MIMALLOC=0. The finding asserts a definite, unconditional break ('cannot find <mimalloc.h>', 'builds zero tier binaries'), contradicted by the guard and the empirically-0 define. A USE=1 build requires the non-default add_subdirectory(ext)/is_original path (CMakeLists.txt:549/572, conditional), which would break the project's own reference umbrella targets identically - a pre-existing project convention, not a defect this diff introduces in COMDARE_FACADE_PERM_INCLUDES.

Trigger + wrong output are constructible from the code and confirmed by the author's own revert. Include chain (unconditional): profile_run_facade.cpp `#include "profile_run_entry.hpp"` -> profile_run_entry.hpp:23 `#include "source_catalog.hpp"` -> source_catalog.hpp:44 `#include <topics/allocator/topic_allocator_config_set.hpp>` -> axis_06_allocator_registry.hpp:28 `#include "axis_06_allocator_mimalloc.hpp"` (all 22 allocator adapters pulled, no gate). The facade's link/include set omits every adapter target: `target_link_libraries(comdare_profile_run_facade PRIVATE Boost::mp11 comdare_builder_xml_config_parser comdare::workload_driver comdare::anatomy_module_loader)` and `_facade_heavy_includes` = libs/cache_engine[/include|/src|/builder], libs/common[/serialization], tests/unit/thesis_tiere, ${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/generated, axis-generated dirs -- none of the ~15 comdare::adapter::a04_mimalloc..a11 / p07..p30 targets nor any ext/ include root. Those targets are the sole carriers of the needed dirs: adapters/A04-mimalloc/CMakeLists.txt `target_include_directories(comdare_adapter_a04_mimalloc INTERFACE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})` (+ ext/allocator/A04-mimalloc/include). The correct pattern is test_v31_adapters at tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:277-301, which links comdare::adapter::a04_mimalloc, a05_jemalloc, ..., p07_wormhole, p10_surf, ... exactly. Decisive: the author's revert commit fac49e66 (`revert(#230): Phase-1-Andockung zurueckgenommen -- CI-rot`) reverts BOTH commits under review (ce 698977fe / super 5b5dc9c) and states verbatim: '(1) analyse:thesis-data: die Fassade zieht via all_axes_umbrella axis_06_allocator_mimalloc -> <mimalloc.h>; im super-Sub-Build fehlen die ~15 vendored Adapter-Includes (comdare::adapter::a04_mimalloc..a11 + p07..p30, tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:286+)' and 'lokal (Standalone-ce) gruen, aber die super-CI zeigte 2 echte Fehler, die im Standalone-ce nicht sichtbar waren' -- matching the candidate's standalone-vs-super divergence claim and the red analyse:thesis-data job.

result.summary: This review covers the Phase-1 docking of an XML-profile-driven E4 measurement facade (the ce `profile_run_facade` library plus the super `messung_driver` E4 dock), a change the author has since reverted for CI failure. The most severe issues are that the facade does not compile in the super sub-build at all (its CMake omits the vendored allocator/paper adapter include dirs pulled transitively by the axis umbrella, [8]) and that the new E4 dock is a far thinner wrapper than the `run_lazy_150` harness it succeeds — it drops top-level exception handling, the "0 valid profiles" hard abort, RAM admission, platform/build CSV tagging, cap-parse validation, and the SOTA opt-out — so an opt-in multi-day thesis run can silently emit scientifically-invalid or platform-mislabeled data, blow past its intended build cap, OOM, or abort past the fallback it explicitly promises to preserve. The remaining findings are lower-confidence, config-dependent build/robustness edge cases and copy-paste/altitude cleanups in the facade's CMake and its hand-rolled g++ compile-fn.
